conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Mr. ___? I'm Dr. ___ from the medical team. You're in the ICU now. You came in because you were having a lot of trouble breathing. Can you tell me how you're feeling right now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I can’t catch my breath… even with this mask. It’s been getting worse for days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I know it’s hard. You’re on BiPAP to help support your breathing. We’ve started you on steroids and nebulizers. Your oxygen is improving. Do you remember why you waited to come in?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I was drinking… trying to calm down. I didn’t want to end up back here again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Your alcohol level was high when you arrived. We’re monitoring you for withdrawal, but your fast heart rate is likely from both the albuterol and anxiety. We’ll keep you comfortable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My stomach’s been killing me too. It’s been bad for weeks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your exam shows tenderness in the upper abdomen. Given your history, we’re concerned it might be related to your CMV gastritis. Are you still taking your valganciclovir?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I stopped it a few days ago. I ran out and didn’t refill it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that could explain the flare-up. We’ve restarted it at a lower dose for maintenance. We also checked for infections—your flu and other virus tests came back negative.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not the flu? Good. But why do I keep having these asthma attacks?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We don’t know yet. Your IgE level was normal, so allergies might not be the main trigger. We’re ruling out other causes. You’ve had a chest X-ray—no pneumonia. But it did show some fluid buildup in the lungs, possibly from heart strain or fluid overload.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My legs are swollen too. Is that related?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your cirrhosis likely contributes. We checked your legs for clots—no DVT. Your heart function from a past echo was okay, so we think the swelling is from liver disease. We’re continuing your diuretics.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my liver? I remember something about a nodule.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, from your last MRCP, there’s a 6.2 cm nodule in your liver. It’s concerning. You need follow-up with hepatology in two months for repeat imaging. We’re not restarting your nadolol yet because of your breathing, but talk to your PCP about it later.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay… I’ll try to make it. I’ve missed a lot before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re here to help. You’re doing better already. Your breathing is less labored. We’ll move you to the floor tomorrow if you keep improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’re off BiPAP now and on room air. Your oxygen is 96%. How’s your breathing?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Much better. Still a little wheezy, but I can talk full sentences now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great progress. We’re spacing out your nebulizers. We also checked your immune levels—your IgG is low, which makes sense with long-term steroids. That’s why you’re prone to CMV and other infections.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So the steroids are helping my asthma but hurting my immunity?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. That’s why we’re giving you atovaquone to prevent pneumonia while you’re on the steroid taper. You’ll stop it once the prednisone is done.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: How long is the taper?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Sixty milligrams for one more day, then 40 mg for five days, 20 mg for five, then 10 mg for five. It’s important to finish it to avoid a rebound flare.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. What about my stomach pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We believe it’s from the CMV gastritis. You’re on valganciclovir once daily now for three months. We’ll stop the IV pain meds. You can restart your Suboxone at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been clean for six months. I just drank because I couldn’t breathe.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. But alcohol can worsen both your liver and asthma. We’re glad you’re committed. Your pulmonologist will want to see you soon—maybe a sleep study too, for CPAP.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had trouble sleeping. Snoring a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s common with asthma and obesity. The sleep team will help. You may also need allergy testing after the steroids are done.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs are stable. Platelets are still low, but that’s expected with cirrhosis. No signs of infection. How’s your skin? We added a steroid cream for your eczema.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It’s better. Less itchy. Thanks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’re planning to discharge you tomorrow if all goes well. You’ll need several follow-ups: pulmonology, sleep medicine, and liver clinic.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a lot. Will they call me?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, pulmonology will call to schedule. The others are set. And please call your Suboxone doctor if you run low before your appointment.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I don’t want to go back to using.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re making good choices. One more thing—your asthma keeps flaring, and we don’t know why. After the taper, you may need a neck CT to check for airway collapse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Airway collapse? Like my throat closing?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not exactly. Tracheobronchomalacia—weak airways that narrow when you breathe out. It can mimic asthma. It’s just a possibility we need to check.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll do it. I just want to breathe normally.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—your breathing is at baseline. We’re discharging you today. Let’s go over your meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’m ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll continue your inhalers, omeprazole, and diuretics. Prednisone taper as we discussed. Valganciclovir once daily for three months. Atovaquone daily until the steroids are done.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And Suboxone?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, restart today. Call your provider if you need more before your appointment. Nadolol is on hold—check with your PCP when it’s safe to restart.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Any restrictions?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Avoid alcohol completely. Watch for worsening breathing, fever, or severe abdominal pain. If any of those happen, come back right away.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for helping me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. You’ve worked hard. Keep up the progress. The nurse will give you your prescriptions and instructions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll make the appointments. I want to stay healthy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick check before you leave. How are you feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Tired, but I can breathe. Ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re cleared to go. Remember your follow-ups and the prednisone schedule. We’re rooting for you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll follow through. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care, Mr. ___. Call us if you need anything.
